title: Bounce animation with exact parabolic arcs
purpose: Key a bouncing motion on the active object from drop height, restitution and gravity: exact parabolic arcs, decaying rebounds, constant travel and optional squash at contacts. Use it for balls, props and motion tests.

parameters.name: drop_height
parameters.description: Height of the object's lowest point above the ground at the first apex.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Distance from the object origin down to its lowest point; measured when measure_radius.

parameters.name: measure_radius
parameters.description: Measure the radius from the active object's bounding box instead of using radius.

parameters.name: restitution
parameters.description: Rebound speed divided by impact speed.

parameters.name: fps
parameters.description: Frames per second; the operator fills it from the scene.

parameters.name: bounces
parameters.description: Most rebounds to key after the first contact.

parameters.name: min_height
parameters.description: Stop when a rebound apex would be lower than this.

parameters.name: squash
parameters.description: Vertical squash at the first contact, scaled down with impact speed for later contacts.

outputs.description: Keyframes on the active object: location Z with free handles, location X linear, scale squash keys.

limits: Point-mass free fall with a constant restitution: no air drag, spin, rolling or deformation physics. The squash is a stylized scale key at each contact, scaled with impact speed, and it lowers the contact key by radius times squash so the object stays on the ground. Motion is along +X on a flat ground only. Keys sit on fractional frames. Verified in Blender 5.2.1, where F-curves live in the action's channel bag; the 4.2 code path uses action.fcurves and was not run.
technique_references: Free fall: t = sqrt(2 h / g), apex height times restitution squared per bounce
Degree elevation of a quadratic Bezier to a cubic: handles at one third of the span
Cubic Bezier F-curve evaluation by solving for the curve parameter
Volume-preserving squash: scale z by 1 - s and x, y by 1 / sqrt(1 - s)
